correctness.rationale: The frozen rational equation and labeled cusp-field theorem are false for Auffarth's canonical model. At the standard X_1(5) infinity cusp the marked point is ζ_5 modulo sign, so the residue field is Q(√5); the frozen Q(t) split at infinity. The complete replacement identifies the ordinary marked-point model via rational Tate normal form. With k=b−11−1/b it gives Δ=b⁶k and j=(k²+10k+5)³/k. Comparing cusp pole orders and leading coefficients on X_0(5) gives t=125/k, and (t/5)(b+1/b) squares to 5Q(t). Forgetting the generator modulo H is this level-five base change, geometrically connected by the surjective character of Γ_0(4800). The residual equations are split at zero and give √5 at infinity; cyclotomic K_d already contains √5 at v_5(d)=1 and excludes it at v_5(d)=2. Thus the corrected criterion is split at depths 0 and 1, nonsplit at depth 2 (e.g. d=1 has two rational lifts; d=25 one quadratic lift). The histogram is unchanged because the extreme strata have identical base degree profiles, so the frozen check of the histogram did not detect the wrong twist. Over the two simple elliptic values, ramification index two at level 4800 yields 960 distinct lifts apiece; the pole divisor pulls back with degree 1920. Multiplying by 5 does not affect the even divisor, so the explicit rational 2-torsion class survives and is geometrically nonprincipal by connectedness. The canonical cover uses the corrected trivialization, not just the underlying line bundle. The independent replacement program was run and passed; no source script was executed.
residual_risks: Finite checks confirm symbolic invariants and the denominator enumeration, not the moduli interpretation or full rational torsion. Those are respectively proved in the corrected argument and outside its scope.

originality.rationale: The surviving distinction is an explicit canonically normalized rational covering equation on the named modular curve together with the labeled residue-field rule and its explicit elliptic-fiber divisor representative. The genus and complex étale cover, geometric cusp count, general cusp orbit theory, and abstract production of a torsion line bundle from a cover are credited to prior results or standard theory. The numerical histogram is a downstream enumeration, not an independent novelty claim. In particular the unnormalized Rogers–Ramanujan equality is not a new equation for the canonical model.
residual_risks: The literature comparison does not settle whether a prior exact standard-model formula or an equivalent Shimura-subgroup divisor representative is listed elsewhere. General intermediate-cusp methods make the enumeration routine once the model and local normalization are supplied, and are not claimed here.

value.rationale: For the specified high-genus modular model, two rational forms have the same geometry and census but different labeled fibers, even above rational base cusps. A researcher using its rational boundary or the associated descent line bundle needs to know which lifts actually split, not just that there are sixteen rational cusps or that the cover is étale. The corrected equation gives those local data and an explicit global representative for the cover class on the lower curve. No independent value is assigned to checking the histogram twice or to the abstract existence of 2-torsion.
residual_risks: Does not determine rational points away from the cusps, full rational Jacobian torsion or the Prym decomposition.
